title: Big Tech earnings week opens with $725B in AI capex and investors looking for the free-cash-flow bill
subtitle: Microsoft and Alphabet report Wednesday after the close; Apple, Amazon and Meta follow by week's end. Meta's $34.9B Q3 capex and negative free cash flow last week set the mood, and the Fed decides rates the same day.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: The four US hyperscalers — Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta — are now on course for roughly $725 billion of combined 2026 capital expenditure, almost all of it AI infrastructure. The quarterly check comes this week. Microsoft and Alphabet report Wednesday October 28 after the US close, with consensus of about $90.6B revenue and $4.71 adjusted EPS for Microsoft, and $127.9B and $3.03 for Alphabet. Apple, Amazon, and Meta follow Thursday and Friday. The Federal Reserve rate decision lands the same Wednesday. Meta's October 21 report set the tone: revenue up 26% to $64.6B, Q3 capex of $34.9B, free cash flow turning negative, and 2026 guidance raised to $135–145B. The stock dropped roughly 13% on the week.

The number investors are chasing has shifted. For most of the year the question was Azure growth and Google Cloud backlog — demand metrics. This quarter it is free cash flow. Capex at this scale, deployed in equipment that depreciates fast, pulls cash out of the business before any new AI revenue books. Microsoft's commercial remaining performance obligations stood around $678 billion the last we saw them, Alphabet's cloud backlog around $514 billion, so the demand side is not the worry. The worry is whether the deployment pace plus the GPU depreciation schedule leaves the balance sheet with room to absorb another leg up. Alphabet's buyback has already been paused.

The context behind the capex number is who gets paid. The four hyperscalers' $725B of 2026 outlay is why TSMC's October quarter printed $46.7B, why Nvidia closed at $217 on October 15 despite a reported OpenAI revenue miss, and why AMD's MI455X 'Helios' racks are at HPE and Microsoft's Maia 300 is scheduled for 2027. The AI-cycle debate — bubble or build-out — comes down to whether the operating income of the customers (OpenAI, Anthropic, agent startups, enterprise AI programs) ever catches the capex of the providers. Earnings week is where that gap gets re-priced, line item by line item.

A note for learners: when you read these reports Wednesday, skip the headlines about EPS beats and go to two numbers. Operating cash flow minus capex is free cash flow — the actual cash left over to pay for buybacks, debt, or dividends. And the breakdown between 'servers and networking' and 'property and buildings' tells you whether the money is chasing GPUs or breaking ground on sites that will take two years to populate. These two line items are what the AI cycle is actually made of. The press release is marketing; the 10-Q cash flow statement is the business.
